statement: U.S. export restrictions have pushed DeepSeek into an architectural split: training stays on whatever Nvidia hardware it can secure while inference moves to Huawei 950DT chips.
why: It shows export controls are now reshaping workload placement rather than just headline revenue, permanently shrinking the Chinese share of merchant GPU inference demand.

impact.mechanism: Controls block Nvidia inference sales into China, so the inference workload migrates to domestic silicon and only the harder-to-substitute training tier keeps buying merchant GPUs.

evidence.excerpt: U.S. restrictions on advanced Nvidia chip sales to China have forced this architectural split between training (still Nvidia-dependent) and inference (shifting to domestic Huawei silicon)

confidence.basis: Single secondary outlet; qualitative characterisation rather than disclosed policy or filing data.
